title: Adult Cardiac Arrest
blurb: VF/pVT · Asystole · PEA — CPR cycles, shocks, epinephrine timing

start.title: Start CPR
bullets: — begin high-quality compressions immediately
Give oxygen — bag-mask ventilation
Attach monitor / defibrillator
start.detail: Compress 2–2.4 in (5–6 cm) at 100–120/min with full recoil; minimize interruptions (target chest-compression fraction > 80%). Rotate compressors every 2 minutes. 30:2 with bag-mask; avoid excessive ventilation.

rhythm1.title: Rhythm check
rhythm1.question: Is the rhythm shockable?
rhythm1.detail: Pause compressions < 10 seconds for the rhythm check. VF = chaotic fibrillation, no organized QRS. pVT = organized wide-complex tachycardia without a pulse. PEA = organized rhythm without a pulse. If in doubt between fine VF and asystole, resume CPR — do not delay compressions.

vf.title: VF / pVT
bullets: Shockable rhythm confirmed — charge the defibrillator while CPR continues

shock1.title: Shock
bullets: manufacturer recommendation (120–200 J); if unknown, use maximum available
Resume CPR immediately after the shock — do not pause for a rhythm check
shock1.detail: Charge during compressions, clear only to deliver. Second and subsequent doses should be equivalent or higher. Restart compressions the moment the shock is delivered.

cpr4.title: CPR 2 min
bullets: High-quality compressions — rotate compressor

shock5.title: Shock
bullets: Equivalent or higher energy than the previous shock

cpr6.title: CPR 2 min
bullets: Consider advanced airway, waveform capnography

meds.name: Epinephrine
meds.detail: 1 mg (10 mL of 0.1 mg/mL) IV/IO push, flush with 20 mL. Repeat every 3–5 minutes. For nonshockable rhythms give as soon as feasible — earlier epinephrine in asystole/PEA is associated with improved ROSC and survival. Follow each peripheral dose with a fluid flush and elevate the limb.

cpr6.detail: With an advanced airway: continuous compressions + 1 breath every 6 seconds (10/min). Waveform capnography confirms tube placement and tracks CPR quality — if ETCO₂ is low or falling, improve compressions.

shock7.title: Shock
bullets: Refractory VF/pVT — consider changing pad vector; DSED may be considered where two defibrillators are available
shock7.detail: 2025 guidance: for VF refractory to standard defibrillation, a change in pad orientation (anterior-posterior) or double sequential external defibrillation (DSED) may be considered.

cpr8.title: CPR 2 min
bullets: or
Treat reversible causes — H's & T's

meds.name: Amiodarone
meds.detail: First dose 300 mg IV/IO bolus (diluted in 20–30 mL D5W). Second dose 150 mg after 3–5 min if VF/pVT persists. For shock-refractory VF/pVT after the 3rd shock. Do not combine with lidocaine — choose one agent.

meds.name: Lidocaine
meds.detail: First dose 1–1.5 mg/kg IV/IO. Second dose 0.5–0.75 mg/kg after 5–10 min (maximum cumulative 3 mg/kg). Alternative to amiodarone for shock-refractory VF/pVT.

meds.name: Magnesium
meds.detail: 1–2 g IV/IO diluted in 10 mL D5W over 5–20 min — only for torsades de pointes with prolonged QT. Not recommended routinely in cardiac arrest.

meds.name: Epinephrine
meds.detail: 1 mg (10 mL of 0.1 mg/mL) IV/IO push, flush with 20 mL. Repeat every 3–5 minutes. For nonshockable rhythms give as soon as feasible — earlier epinephrine in asystole/PEA is associated with improved ROSC and survival. Follow each peripheral dose with a fluid flush and elevate the limb.

cpr8.detail: Antiarrhythmic for shock-refractory VF/pVT (typically after the 3rd shock). Keep epinephrine on its 3–5 min schedule. Actively work the H's & T's checklist — open the Causes panel and mark what you have excluded.

asystole.title: Asystole / PEA
bullets: — as soon as feasible
Confirm asystole in more than one lead; check gain and connections

meds.name: Epinephrine
meds.detail: 1 mg (10 mL of 0.1 mg/mL) IV/IO push, flush with 20 mL. Repeat every 3–5 minutes. For nonshockable rhythms give as soon as feasible — earlier epinephrine in asystole/PEA is associated with improved ROSC and survival. Follow each peripheral dose with a fluid flush and elevate the limb.

asystole.detail: Early epinephrine in nonshockable arrest improves ROSC and survival — do not wait for the next cycle boundary. True asystole must be distinguished from fine VF and lead disconnection.

cpr10.title: CPR 2 min
bullets: Consider advanced airway, capnography

meds.name: Epinephrine
meds.detail: 1 mg (10 mL of 0.1 mg/mL) IV/IO push, flush with 20 mL. Repeat every 3–5 minutes. For nonshockable rhythms give as soon as feasible — earlier epinephrine in asystole/PEA is associated with improved ROSC and survival. Follow each peripheral dose with a fluid flush and elevate the limb.

cpr11.title: CPR 2 min
bullets: Treat reversible causes — H's & T's
Continue epinephrine every 3–5 min

meds.name: Epinephrine
meds.detail: 1 mg (10 mL of 0.1 mg/mL) IV/IO push, flush with 20 mL. Repeat every 3–5 minutes. For nonshockable rhythms give as soon as feasible — earlier epinephrine in asystole/PEA is associated with improved ROSC and survival. Follow each peripheral dose with a fluid flush and elevate the limb.

cpr11.detail: PEA is a 'why' rhythm — survival depends on finding the cause. Narrow-complex PEA suggests a mechanical cause (tamponade, tension pneumothorax, PE, hypovolemia); wide-complex suggests metabolic (hyperkalemia, toxins).

rosc-check.title: ROSC assessment
rosc-check.question: Signs of return of spontaneous circulation?
bullets: Pulse and blood pressure
Abrupt sustained rise in ETCO₂ (typically ≥ 40 mm Hg)
Spontaneous arterial waveform on intra-arterial monitoring
rosc-check.detail: If no ROSC: continue cycles and consider the appropriateness of continued resuscitation — team consensus, downtime, ETCO₂ persistently < 10 mm Hg after 20 min of good CPR, and reversible-cause status all inform the decision. Consider ECPR (extracorporeal CPR) in selected patients with a reversible cause where a program exists.

rosc.title: Post-Cardiac Arrest Care
bullets: Manage airway; SpO₂ 90–98% (PaO₂ 60–105), PaCO₂ 35–45 mm Hg
Maintain MAP ≥ 65 mm Hg — vasopressors and/or fluids
12-lead ECG — emergent cath if STEMI
Temperature control; EEG if not following commands
rosc.detail: Open the Post-Cardiac Arrest Care algorithm for the full walkthrough.

title: Pediatric Cardiac Arrest
blurb: Weight-based dosing · 2→4 J/kg shocks · 15:2 ratios — set patient weight for computed doses

start.title: Start CPR
bullets: — ≥ ⅓ AP chest diameter at 100–120/min
Begin bag-mask ventilation and give oxygen
Attach monitor / defibrillator
start.detail: Compression-ventilation ratios: 15:2 with 2 rescuers (prepuberty); 30:2 with 2 rescuers (postpuberty onset); 30:2 with 1 rescuer at any age. Full recoil, rotate compressor every 2 minutes. Monitor ETCO₂ and, when available, invasive diastolic BP.

vf.title: VF / pVT
bullets: Shockable rhythm confirmed — charge the defibrillator while CPR continues

shock1.title: Shock ASAP
bullets: Resume CPR immediately after the shock
shock1.detail: Energy sequence: first shock 2 J/kg, second 4 J/kg, subsequent ≥ 4 J/kg to a maximum of 10 J/kg or the adult dose.

cpr4.title: CPR 2 min
bullets: High-quality compressions — rotate compressor

cpr6.detail: With an advanced airway in place: continuous compressions and give a breath every 2–3 seconds (20–30 breaths/min).

title: Adult Bradycardia With a Pulse
blurb: HR < 50 with a pulse — atropine, pacing, chronotropic infusions

b1.title: Recognize bradycardia
bullets: if bradyarrhythmia
Assess appropriateness for the clinical condition
b1.detail: Common causes: myocardial ischemia/infarction; drugs/toxicologic (calcium-channel blockers, β-blockers, digoxin); hypoxia; electrolyte abnormality (e.g. hyperkalemia). Treat the cause in parallel with the rhythm.

b2.title: Cardiopulmonary compromise?
b2.question: Bradyarrhythmia causing any of: hypotension · acutely altered mental status · signs of shock · ischemic chest discomfort · acute heart failure?

b3.title: Identify causes · observe
bullets: Identify and treat underlying causes
Support ABCs · consider oxygen
Obtain 12-lead ECG
Observe — reassess if symptoms develop
b3.detail: Common causes: myocardial ischemia/infarction; drugs (CCB, β-blocker, digoxin); hypoxia; electrolyte abnormality (e.g. hyperkalemia).

b4.title: Assessment and support
bullets: Maintain patent airway and provide oxygen
Assist breathing with positive-pressure ventilation as necessary
Attach cardiorespiratory monitor · monitor pulse
IV access · 12-lead ECG if it does not delay therapy

b5.title: Persistence check
b5.question: Does bradycardia persist with cardiopulmonary compromise?

b6.title: Atropine → pacing / infusion
bullets: — repeat every 3–5 min · maximum 3 mg
If atropine ineffective:
— and/or
5–20 mcg/kg/min — or
2–10 mcg/min

meds.name: Atropine
meds.dose: 1 mg IV — repeat q3–5 min, max 3 mg
meds.detail: 1 mg IV bolus, may repeat every 3–5 minutes to a maximum total of 3 mg. Likely ineffective in high-grade (Mobitz II / third-degree) block with wide QRS — move to pacing/chronotropes early. Avoid relying on atropine in cardiac transplant patients (denervated heart).

meds.name: Dopamine gtt
meds.detail: Infusion 5–20 mcg/kg/min IV; titrate to heart rate and blood pressure. Taper slowly.

meds.name: Epinephrine gtt
meds.detail: Infusion 2–10 mcg/min IV; titrate to patient response. Bridge to pacing when available.

b6.detail: Do not delay pacing for atropine in high-grade AV block (Mobitz II / third-degree, wide QRS) — atropine is unlikely to work at or below the His bundle. For TCP: confirm electrical AND mechanical capture (femoral pulse), set rate ~60–80/min and output 10–20 mA above capture threshold; sedate/analgese the conscious patient.

b7.title: Consider
bullets: Expert consultation (cardiology)
Transvenous pacing
If arrest develops — switch to the Cardiac Arrest algorithm

title: Adult Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse
blurb: HR ≥ 150 with a pulse — cardioversion, adenosine, antiarrhythmics

t1.title: Assess & support
bullets: if tachyarrhythmia
Assess appropriateness for clinical condition — rule out sinus tachycardia from fever, pain, hypovolemia, sepsis
Maintain airway; oxygen if hypoxemic
Cardiac monitor · blood pressure · oximetry · IV access
12-lead ECG if available — don't delay cardioversion if unstable

t2.title: Stability check
t2.question: Persistent tachyarrhythmia causing any of: hypotension · acutely altered mental status · signs of shock · ischemic chest discomfort · acute heart failure?

t3.title: Synchronized cardioversion
bullets: — but do not delay cardioversion in decompensation
use the device's recommended level to maximize first-shock success; if unknown, use maximum available (2025)
If regular narrow complex, consider adenosine while preparing

meds.name: Adenosine
meds.detail: First dose 6 mg rapid IV push via large (antecubital) vein followed by immediate 20 mL NS flush; second dose 12 mg if required. Use only for regular rhythms (narrow, or wide AND regular + monomorphic). Warn the patient about transient chest pressure / impending-doom sensation.

t3.detail: Press SYNC before every shock (it resets after each delivery on most devices). If the device won't sync on a very fast polymorphic rhythm, treat as VF with an unsynchronized high-energy shock. If cardioversion fails, increase energy stepwise and consider an antiarrhythmic infusion and expert consultation. Classic initial energies: narrow regular 50–100 J · narrow irregular 120–200 J biphasic · wide regular 100 J · wide irregular — defibrillation dose (unsynchronized).

t5.title: Stable wide-QRS
bullets: Consider
only if regular AND monomorphic
Consider

meds.name: Adenosine
meds.detail: First dose 6 mg rapid IV push via large (antecubital) vein followed by immediate 20 mL NS flush; second dose 12 mg if required. Use only for regular rhythms (narrow, or wide AND regular + monomorphic). Warn the patient about transient chest pressure / impending-doom sensation.

meds.name: Procainamide gtt
meds.detail: 20–50 mg/min until arrhythmia suppressed, hypotension, QRS widens > 50%, or max 17 mg/kg. Maintenance 1–4 mg/min. Avoid in prolonged QT or CHF.

meds.name: Amiodarone gtt
meds.detail: First dose 150 mg over 10 minutes; repeat as needed if VT recurs. Maintenance 1 mg/min for the first 6 hours.

t5.detail: Treat undifferentiated regular wide-complex tachycardia as VT. Never give AV-nodal blockers (verapamil/diltiazem/β-blockers) to a wide, irregular, very fast rhythm — pre-excited AF can degenerate to VF.

t6.title: Stable narrow-QRS
bullets: — modified Valsalva ~40 mm Hg 15 s with leg raise
if regular — 6 mg → 12 mg rapid push
Consider expert consultation

meds.name: Adenosine
meds.detail: First dose 6 mg rapid IV push via large (antecubital) vein followed by immediate 20 mL NS flush; second dose 12 mg if required. Use only for regular rhythms (narrow, or wide AND regular + monomorphic). Warn the patient about transient chest pressure / impending-doom sensation.

meds.name: Diltiazem
meds.detail: 0.25 mg/kg IV over 2 min; may repeat 0.35 mg/kg after 15 min. Then 5–15 mg/h infusion. Avoid in hypotension or reduced EF.

meds.name: Metoprolol
meds.detail: 5 mg slow IV push over 1–2 min, repeat every 5 minutes to a total of 15 mg as tolerated.

t6.detail: Adenosine both converts AVNRT/AVRT and unmasks atrial flutter. Record a continuous rhythm strip during administration. For AF/flutter, the goal is rate control (CCB/β-blocker) — cardioversion decisions depend on anticoagulation status and duration.

t7.title: Reassess
bullets: Reassess rhythm, perfusion, and symptoms after each intervention
If the patient becomes unstable — synchronized cardioversion
If pulse is lost — switch to the Cardiac Arrest algorithm
If refractory: address underlying cause; increase energy for the next cardioversion; add an antiarrhythmic; expert consultation

title: Adult Post–Cardiac Arrest Care
blurb: After ROSC — oxygenation, hemodynamics, cath decisions, temperature control

p1.title: Initial stabilization after ROSC
bullets: assess; place or exchange an advanced airway as necessary; confirm placement (waveform capnography)
100% FiO₂ until SpO₂/PaO₂ can be measured reliably, then titrate to SpO₂ 90–98% (PaO₂ 60–105 mm Hg)
target PaCO₂ 35–45 mm Hg (unless severe acidemia)
target MAP ≥ 65 mm Hg — vasopressors and/or fluid resuscitation
p1.detail: Resuscitation is ongoing during the post-ROSC phase and many of these activities occur concurrently. Even brief hypotension after ROSC worsens neurological outcome — treat aggressively.

p2.title: Early diagnostic testing
bullets: Obtain a 12-lead ECG — assess for ischemia or arrhythmia
Consider CT head / chest / abdomen–pelvis for cause of arrest or resuscitation injuries
Point-of-care ultrasound or echocardiography may identify significant diagnoses
Labs: ABG, lactate, electrolytes incl. K⁺/Mg²⁺, troponin, glucose

p3.title: Emergency cardiac intervention?
p3.question: Persistent ST-segment elevation · cardiogenic shock · recurrent/refractory ventricular arrhythmias · severe myocardial ischemia?
p3.detail: Treat arrest etiologies and complications. Consider emergency coronary angiography and/or mechanical circulatory support for the indications above.

p4.title: Emergency cardiac intervention
bullets: Activate the cath lab — emergency coronary angiography ± PCI
Consider mechanical circulatory support
Continue neuroprotective care in parallel

p5.title: Neurological assessment
p5.question: Off sedation and neuromuscular blockade (if able) — does the patient follow commands?

p6.title: Comatose pathway
bullets: deliberate strategy with goal 32–37.5 °C, started as soon as possible; actively prevent fever
evaluate for clinical seizure; obtain EEG in patients not following commands
Coronary angiography when appropriate
multimodal, appropriately timed — ≥ 72 h from ROSC or achieving normothermia
p6.detail: No single early finding is sufficient for prognosis — use a delayed, multimodal approach and avoid premature pessimism in the first days.

p7.title: Ongoing critical care
bullets: Target PaO₂ 60–105 mm Hg · PaCO₂ 35–45 mm Hg (unless severe acidemia) · MAP ≥ 65 mm Hg
Avoid hypoglycemia (< 70 mg/dL) and hyperglycemia (> 180 mg/dL)
Consider antibiotics · coronary angiography when appropriate
ICU admission — treat the precipitating cause; early cardiology/neurology involvement
